description: One OptionParser.parse call builds 538,281 hash tables for 2,570 jobs and makes 2.2M hash calls; 73% of the tables are empty when dropped, 95% hold four entries or fewer. Removing tables and hashing that should not exist saves 8-12% of release instructions; a faster seeded hasher on what remains brings it to 20-24% (measured cumulatively, outputs identical). Proposal page: /Users/j5n/Workspace/compile-cost-round-two.html (https://claude.ai/artifact/4T5Lime7pQxKbCiKJqaJ8x). Spike (base c768670cd; port by reading, not by applying): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b3126377-4731-4b0b-825a-a57f770f6d53/scratchpad/tables/ results.md, step0_sites.md, predictions.md. Not yet measured: where the remaining ~2.9M allocations per parse call come from; per-kind id-indexed fact/product/dependency tables (needs its own page).
title: The compiler builds a table only where a table is the right structure
